May

16 May

  • Gaza health officials said that over 100 people including women and children were killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza.[1][2][3]
  • The IDF said that it conducted airstrikes on more than 150 militant targets including anti-tank missile launch posts, cells and buildings used to conduct attacks on its forces. It also said that it killed several militants who were at an observation post during ground operations in north Gaza, destroyed several tunnel shafts and other infrastructure and killed several militants during ground operations in Rafah and killed militants attempting to plant a bomb in the Morag Corridor.[4]
  • The IDF said that it conducted attacks on Hudaydah Port and Port of Salif in response to Houthi attacks on Israel, and destroyed infrastructure at ports controlled by Houthis and used for weapons transfers. The Houthi-controlled Health Ministry stated that one person was killed and nine others were wounded in the airstrikes.[5][6][7]
  • Israeli forces issued evacuation orders for residents of Gaza to move south.[8]
  • UN's Interim Forces in Lebanon (UNIFIL) said that a “large group of individuals” confronted UN troops in South Lebanon during a routine patrol and called the Lebanese government to ensure there are no obstructions to the peacekeeping force.[9]
  • An Israeli police officer was injured in a stabbing attack in the Old City of Jerusalem. The attacker was shot dead by Israeli police.[10]

17 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 153 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,272.[11][a]
  • Israeli forces announced that they started a major offensive in Gaza.[12]
  • The IDF said that it downed a drone apparently launched by the Houthis.[13]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a vehicle carrying people evacuating from eastern Khan Yunis, killing an elderly man and his two grandchildren.[14]
  • One person was killed in an Israeli drone strike on a car in Tyre District. The IDF said that it killed a Hezbollah commander who was involved in restoring Hezbollah's capabilities in the Beaufort Castle area.[15][16]
  • Gaza rescuers said that an Israeli strike hit a tent west of Khan Yunis, killing one person and injuring five others including a girl, a young woman and a pregnant woman.[17]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a house in Jabalia, killing four children.[18]
  • The IDF said that it destroyed a "strategic" Hamas tunnel measuring 2 km while operating in north Gaza.[19]
  • Al Jazeera reported that IDF fire hit an elderly Palestinian man in the vicinity of the entrance to Jenin refugee camp, injuring him.[20]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit Deir el-Balah, killing nine family members including three children.[21]

18 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 67 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,339.[22][a]
  • The IDF said that it downed a ballistic missile fired towards Israel by the Houthis. Israeli media outlet Channel 12 reported, citing the IDF that a second unsuccessful missile launch was attempted from Yemen. The Houthis said that they launched a hypersonic Palestine 2 missile and a Zulfiqar missile towards Ben Gurion Airport.[23][24][25]
  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that least 151 Palestinians, including children were killed in Israeli strikes in Gaza.[26][27][12]
  • Al Jazeera reported that at least five more Palestinian journalists were included among those killed in Israeli strikes in recent days.[28]
  • Gaza media outlets reported that a lecturer who was the brother of former Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar and de facto leader of Hamas in the Gaza Strip Muhammad Sinwar was seriously wounded in an airstrike which hit a tent in Nuseirat along with his three children.[29][30]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli drone hit a car in the vicinity of a Lebanese army checkpoint in Beit Yahoun, injuring two people including a Lebanese soldier.[31]
  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that all public hospitals in north Gaza went out of service.[32]
  • The IDF announced that it started a "broad" ground offensive in Gaza. It said that the IAF launched strikes on 670 Hamas targets in the last week including weapons depots, militant cells, tunnels and anti-tank launch sites, killed dozens of militants, destroyed militant infrastructure, and holding "strategic" areas in Gaza,[33] using five divisions.[34]
  • The IDF said that it downed one rocket fired from central Gaza towards Kissufim, while another rocket hit an open area. al-Qassam Brigades said that it launched the rockets. It later warned residents to evacuate from Al-Qarara suburb of Khan Yunis and southern Deir al-Balah.[35][36][37]
  • Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that "basic amount" of food will be allowed into Gaza after blocking aid for more than two months.[38][39][40]
  • An Israeli strike hit a tent on Al-Barakah Street in Deir al-Balah, killing a Palestinian woman.[37][41]

19 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 136 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,486.[42][a]
  • At least 126 Palestinians including civilians were killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza.[43][44]
  • Wafa reported that a Palestinian boy was severely beaten and detained by Israeli forces in Beit Ummar.[45]
  • A commander of the Al-Nasser Salah al-Deen Brigades was killed in a clash with Israeli special forces in Khan Yunis. Israeli forces also detained his wife and child.[46][47]
  • The IDF said that Israeli warplanes struck more than 160 targets in Gaza in the last day including militant cells, anti-tank missile launch sites, tunnels, a weapons depot, buildings used by militant groups, booby-trapped structures and a command center.[48]
  • The IDF issed evacuation orders for Palestinians in Khan Yunis, Bani Suheila and Abasan al-Kabira to move to al-Mawasi before it launches an "unprecedented attack". It also declared the entirety of Khan Yunis as a combat zone.[49]
  • The IDF said that it destroyed a tunnel used by Hamas for an attack which killed two soldiers on 3 May in Rafah.[50]
  • An Israeli strike hit a school sheltering displaced people in Nuseirat, killing at least seven Palestinians, including a woman and a young girl and wounded 18 others including children. The IDF said that it targeted Hamas militants in a command center in the school.[51][52]
  • The al-Qassam Brigades claimed that several Israeli troops were killed and injured in an ambush in Atatra, Beit Lahia.[53]
  • A 16-year-old Palestinian was detained after clashes between residents and Israeli forces in Sa'ir.[54]
  • Three UNRWA employees were killed in Gaza.[55]
  • One person was killed in an Israeli drone attack in Houla. The IDF said that it killed a Redwan force militant. Three people were injured in two other incidents in the vicinity of the Lebanese border.[56][57]
  • The IDF announced that a soldier from 601st Combat Engineering Battalion was killed while fighting in north Gaza, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 416.[58] An IDF investigation found that he was killed after being hit by friendly fire.[59]
  • Houthis announced a "maritime blockade" against the Port of Haifa.[60]
  • An alleged Hamas militant was arrested in Denmark for purchasing drones to be used in militant attacks.[61]

20 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 87 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,573.[62][a]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a home in Deir el-Balah, killing 12 people and several others went missing.[63]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a petrol station in Nuseirat refugee camp, killing 15 people including children.[64]
  • The Gaza Health Ministry said that an Israeli strikes hit a house and a school serving as shelter in north Gaza, killing at least 22 people including children and women. The IDF said it struck a command center and warned civilians in advance.[65]
  • Al Jazeera reported that Israeli strikes in Khan Yunis refugee camp killed five people including three children.[66]
  • Al Jazeera reported that ten people including a 17-year-old boy were detained by Israeli forces during an operation in the West Bank.[67]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli drone strike on a motorcycle in the vicinity of Majdal Zoun killed one person and injured five others.[68]
  • The IDF said that it struck more than 100 militant targets including a tunnel, a weapons depot, militants, buildings used by militant groups including a building used by PIJ for storing weapons and observation posts. The IDF and Shin Bet also said that they killed the commander of Hamas's aerial forces in north Gaza in a strike three days prior.[69][70]
  • Wafa reported that dozens of people including journalists suffered suffocation during an Israeli operation in Askar al-Qadeem refugee camp, east of Nablus.[71]
  • NNA reported that firing from an Israeli drone hit fishermen in Ras an-Naqoura.[72]
  • A Palestinian paracyclist was among those killed in an Israeli strike on south Gaza.[73]
  • The Hungarian Parliament passed a bill for exiting the International Criminal Court in response to its issuance of arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for alleged war crimes in Gaza.[74]
  • The IDF said that it killed the commander of Hezbollah forces in Al-Mansouri in a drone strike.[75]
  • Al Jazeera reported that at least 326 deaths in Gaza were caused by malnutrition and lack of medicine since Israel's complete blockade started on 2 March.[76]

21 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 82 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,655.[77][a]
  • Hospital officials said that fourteen members from one family including eight children were included among those killed in an Israeli strikes in Khan Yunis.[78][79]
  • AP reported that a one-week-old infant was included among those killed in an Israeli strike in central Gaza.[78]
  • The IDF announced that a soldier from the 51st Company in the 82nd Battalion of the 7th Brigade was killed while another was injured during combat in south Gaza following the collapse of a building where their unit was operating, setting off an explosion, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 417.[80]
  • The UK announced sanctions on far-right Israeli settler Daniella Weiss, whom they called the "godmother" of Israeli settler movements.[81]
  • Lebanese media reported that an Israeli drone hit a vehicle in Ain Baal. The IDF said that it killed “an experienced engineer” in Hezbollah's weapons research and development division.[82][83]
  • Twenty Palestinians including three women were detained by Israeli forces from the West Bank.[84]
  • Israeli forces fired at a diplomatic delegation from foreign nations visiting Jenin refugee camp. The IDF said that it fired warning shots after they deviated from an agreed route. It later apologized.[85][86][87]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli drone hit Yatar, killing one person. The IDF said that it killed a commander of Hezbollah's Radwan force.[88][89]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck more than 115 targets in Gaza in the last day including a drone strike in north Gaza which killed a Nukhba Force militant in its East Jabalia Battalion who participated in the 7 October attacks, rocket launchers, buildings used by militant groups, tunnels, other infrastructure, and militant cells. It added that the Israeli Navy also conducted shelling in north Gaza to assist ground forces operating in the area.[90]
  • The IDF said that it detained a Palestinian suspected of directing the 2025 al-Funduq shooting from western Jenin.[91]
  • The IDF said that air defences downed a rocket fired from north Gaza towards Ashkelon. The PIJ claimed responsibility. The IDF later issued evacuation orders for residents of more than a dozen areas of north Gaza to move south.[92][93]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli strike hit Aitaroun, killing one person. It also reported that several others were injured. The IDF said that it killed a Hezbollah militant.[94][95]
  • The IDF announced that it killed militant who carried out a shooting attack in Brukhin which killed a pregnant Israeli woman and injured her husband on 14 May.[96]
  • The IDF said that three rockets were fired from north Gaza towards Israel, all of which fell short in Gaza.[97]
  • The IDF said that it intercepted a missile fired towards Israel from Yemen.[98]
  • Almost 90 truckloads of aid were collected by UN and dispatched to Gaza after more than two months of total Israeli blockade.[99]

22 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 107 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,762.[100][a]
  • Two hospitals in north Gaza were encircled by Israeli forces, according to hospital staff.[101]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a warehouse sheltering displaced Palestinians in Deir el-Balah, killing at least nine people including a seven-year-old.[102]
  • Three Palestinian prisoners released as part of a hostage agreement including a PIJ militant who was sentenced to a life sentence for his involvement in a shooting which killed a seven-year-old girl in 2003 were rearrested by Israel.[103]
  • The IDF said that it demolished the house of a Palestinian militant who killed an Israeli civilian man during overnight operations in Baqat al-Hatab.[104]
  • The IDF said that it downed a ballistic missile fired towards Israel by the Houthis.[105]
  • The Ministry of Health (Palestine) said that 29 starvation-related deaths in Gaza were registered in Gaza in recent days.[106]
  • A home in the vicinity of entrance to Berin, southeast of Hebron was set on fire by settlers.[107]
  • A 33-year-old Palestinian prisoner died in an Israeli jail.[108]
  • Israeli forces arrested a paramedic and seized an ambulance at a checkpoint east of Ramallah.[109]
  • The IDF warned residents to stay away, and called them to expel Hamas "elements" allegedly hiding in civilian infrastructure, such as a hospital, tent shelters and the municipality in Deir al-Balah. It also named three prominent Hamas militants that are hiding in those areas.[110]
  • Brother of former Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar and de facto leader of Hamas in the Gaza Strip Muhammad Sinwar died from injuries sustained in an Israeli strike five days prior.[111]
  • The IDF said that it intercepted another missile fired towards Israel from Yemen.[111]
  • The IDF said that its 98th Division killed dozens of militants as part of its new offensive in Gaza and demolished almost 200 infrastructures including tunnels.[112]
  • The IDF said that a tank commander from 52nd Battalion of 401st Armored Brigade was critically injured during combat in north Gaza, while another soldier was slightly wounded after a grenade exploded during operations in south Gaza. It said that it killed militants in north Gaza as a response.[113][114]
  • The IDF warned to stay away from a building in Toul, Lebanon, describing it as a Hezbollah facility. It later struck the building.[115][116]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli strike in Rab Thalathin killed one person.[117] The IDF said that it killed a Redwan Force militant in a drone attack.[118]
  • NNA reported that Israeli firing injured a shepherd in Wazzani.[117]
  • The IDF said that it struck a Hezbollah facility used to store weapons in Beqaa Valley.[119]
  • NNA reported Israeli strikes in Soujod, Touline, Sawanna and the Rihan Mountain.[120]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli attack killed at least six Gaza Interior Ministry police members guarding humanitarian aid from looting. The IDF said that it targeted Hamas militants. However, Gaza Government Media Media said that they were “aid security and protection teams … who were performing purely humanitarian tasks”.[121][122][79]
  • Lebanese media reported that Israeli attacks targeted Wadi al-Aziya and Deir Intar. Israeli bombardment also hit two mobile houses in Shamaa.[123]
  • Dozens of Israeli settlers set fire to almost five homes, five vehicles owned by residents and injured eight people in Bruqin.[124][125]
  • Palestinian hospital officials said that Israeli tanks and drones hit Al-Awda Hospital. The IDF said that it operated adjacent to the hospital.[126]

23 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 60 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,822.[127][a]
  • The IDF said that its air defences downed a missile fired by the Houthis towards Israel.[128]
  • Palestinian militants opened fire on Israeli forces in Nablus.[129]
  • Israel Border Police dismantled 27 explosive devices aimed at security personnel, arrested 20 suspects, and confiscated weapons and large amounts of ammunition in the West Bank.[130]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a home in Jabalia, killing three people including two children.[131]
  • Al Jazeera reported that at least 50 people including an infant boy, were killed or trapped under the rubble after an Israeli strike hit a four-story residential building in Jabalia al-Balad area of north Gaza.[132][133]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a home in Qizan an-Najjar, killing eight people including seven children.[134]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck more than 75 targets in Gaza in the last day including militants, rocket launchers, buildings used by militant groups, weapon depots, and other infrastructure. It also said that ground forces killed several militants throughout Gaza and destroyed other Hamas sites.[135]
  • The IDF said that it targeted a currency exchange company funding Hamas and PIJ in overnight airstrikes in Gaza City.[136]
  • The IDF said that air defences downed one rocket fired towards Israel from Gaza.[137]
  • The IDF said it hit 15 Hezbollah targets in Lebanon overnight.[138]
  • Wafa reported that a condolence gathering was stormed by Israeli forces in Hebron.[139]
  • AP reported that an Israeli strike hit a home in Khan Yunis, killing nine children, critically injuring two others including a child and trapping two children under the rubble.[140]

24 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 79 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived in hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,901.[141][a]
  • Al Jazeera reported that Israeli strikes hit a house in the vicinity of al-Qassam Mosque in Nuseirat, killing one Palestinian and injuring five others including a one-month-old infant.[142]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a residential flat in south Gaza, killing four people including a woman and her two children.[143]
  • The IDF said that it shot and injured a Palestinian who tried to stab soldiers at a checkpoint in Hebron.[144]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit the perimeter of Al-Awda Hospital.[145]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck more than 100 targets in Gaza in the last day including a rocket launcher used in an attack on southern Israel.[146]
  • Wafa reported that water pipes supplying Palestinian families were damaged by Israeli settlers in al-Auja waterfall, north of Jericho.[147]
  • Al Jazeera reported that several health workers and others were trapped inside Gaza European Hospital because of repeated Israeli fire.[145]
  • Wafa reported that four hectares of wheat crops were set on fire by Israeli settlers in Sebastia, Nablus.[148]
  • The World Food Programme said that over 70,000 children in Gaza face acute malnutrition.[149]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit the Israeli designated "safe zone" of al-Mawasi, killing seven Palestinians and injuring dozens of others.[150]
  • The IDF said that its entire standing army infantry and armored brigades are now deployed in Gaza.[151]
  • A four-year-old boy died due to starvation in Gaza City.[152]
  • Al Jazeera reported that groups of Israeli settlers attacked Mughayer Al-Deir in the vicinity of Deir Dibwan, injuring five Palestinians.[153]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli settler attack in Kisan, Palestine wounded seven Palestinians.[153]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in the vicinity of European Gaza Hospital killed two children.[154]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a house in Khan Yunis, killing two International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement workers.[155]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an 11-year-old social media influencer was included among those killed in Israeli strikes in Gaza.[156]

25 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 38 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived in hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,939.[157][a]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit the Israeli-designated "safe zone" of al-Mawasi, killing one person and injuring several others.[158]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli settler attack in Al-Maniya wounded seven Palestinians.[159]
  • Israeli settlers attacked vehicles belonging to Palestinians in the vicinity of Kedumim.[159]
  • Peru opened a criminal investigation into an Israeli soldier accused of war crimes in Gaza.[160]
  • Two 16-year-old Palestinian boys were detained by Israeli forces in Al-Khader.[161]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a house in Jabalia an-Nazla, killing seven people including a male journalist.[162]
  • The IDF said that a soldier was critically injured in a fight with another soldier in north Gaza.[163] It later suspended a soldier for beating another soldier as part of an investigation.[164]
  • The IDF said that it downed a missile fired from Yemen at Israel. The Houthis said that they fired a "hypersonic" ballistic missile at Ben Gurion Airport.[165][166]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a tent camp in Deir el-Balah, killing five family members including two children.[167]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a house in Nuseirat refugee camp, killing the operational director of Gaza Civil Defence and his wife.[166]
  • The al-Qassam and al-Quds Brigades said that they conducted several ambushes and attacks with bombs and anti-tank rockets against Israeli forces in several areas throughout Gaza.[168]
  • The IDF said that it killed a Hamas militant who served in its naval commando unit and participated in the 7 October attacks in a recent strike conducted jointly by the Southern Command, the IAF, Aman, the Navy and Shin Bet in Gaza.[169]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a tent in Deir el-Balah, killing a mother and her children.[170]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in Jabalia killed at least five people including two women and a child.[170]
  • An Israeli strike hit Fahmi Al-Jarjawi school sheltering displaced people in Daraj Quarter of Gaza City, killing at least 36 people and injuring dozens including children and women.[171][172][173] The IDF and Shin Bet said that they targeted a Hamas and PIJ compound inside the school.[174]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a tent in Bani Suheila, killing a child and injuring four relatives.[175]

26 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 38 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived in hospitals in Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 53,977.[176][a]
  • Al Jazeera reported that a Palestinian man was beaten and kidnapped by Israeli settlers from Wadi Abu Ijheesh area of Masafer Yatta.[177]
  • Jake Wood, Gaza Humanitarian Foundation's executive director resigned from the post, saying that the foundation could not adhere "to the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, which I will not abandon".[178]
  • Gaza Humanitarian Foundation said that it started aid delivery.[179]
  • Gazans reported that the IDF started ground operations and artillery fire in Deir al-Balah.[180]
  • An Israeli strike hit a house in Jabalia, killing 16 people including five women and two children.[179]
  • The IDF said that three rockets were launched from Gaza at Israeli communities in the vicinity of the border, adding that it downed one of them and two others fell inside Gaza.[181]
  • Israeli forces detained the wife of a wanted Palestinian from Dura, Hebron to force him to surrender.[182]
  • The IDF said the IAF conducted more than 200 strikes in Gaza in last 48 hours. It also said that targets included militants, weapon depots, anti-tank and sniper positions, tunnel shafts, and other infrastructure. It added that its soldiers struck a building used by Hamas as a weapons depot, an observation post, and another structure used by the group, directed drone strikes on several militants spotted in buildings in the vicinity of its forces in south Gaza and launched an airstrike strike on a building where the Nukhba Force was operating in north Gaza.[183]
  • The IDF issued order for Palestinians to evacuate from all of south Gaza excluding Mawasi humanitarian zone, Al-Amal Hospital and Nasser Hospital to move to Mawasi.[184]
  • Lebanese media reported an Israeli strike in the vicinity of Brital.[185]
  • The IDF said that it killed a cell of militants who launched mortars towards it while operating in north Gaza.[186]
  • The al-Qassam Brigades said that it targeted four Israeli soldiers using rocket-propelled grenades in al-Muntar Street of Shuja'iyya. It also said that it targeted several Merkava tanks using Al-Yassin 105 rockets in Shuja'iyya.[187]
  • The IDF called on residents to collaborate in dismantling Hamas by distributing flyers at Al-Shati refugee camp.[188]
  • Lebanese media reported that Israeli ground forces operated in the vicinity of Mais al-Jabal.[189]

27 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 79 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,056.[190][a]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit Al-Karama area of Gaza City, killing a child and wounding others.[191]
  • NNA reported that bulldozing operations were conducted by Israeli forces on the eastern outskirts of Mais al-Jabal.[192]
  • The IDF said that it downed a missile fired by the Houthis at Israel.[193]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an agricultural land was set on fire by Israeli settlers in Haris, Salfit.[194]
  • The IDF said that it shot down another ballistic missile fired towards Israel from Yemen.[195]
  • Israeli forces started raids on money exchange shops throughout the West Bank.[196] The IDF and Israeli police said that they launched an operation aimed at seizing militant funds and detaining the owners of money exchange companies accused by Israel of funneling cash to militant groups.[197] Four people were shot and injured by Israeli forces and tear gas injured 15 others in Nablus during the raid.[198]
  • The al-Qassam Brigades claimed that it inflicted casualties on an Israeli unit of 10 soldiers using an antipersonnel missile in al-Atatra, Beit Lahia.[199]
  • Houthis said that they launched missiles towards Ben Gurion Airport and a "vital target" east of Tel Aviv.[200]
  • Two of four sites for distributing aid were now operational in Gaza.[201][202][203]
  • Palestinian media reported that vehicles were set on fire and houses were damaged by dozens of settlers in Qaryut.[204][205]
  • The IDF said that it killed a Radwan Force militant in a drone strike in Majdal Zoun one day prior.[206]
  • Al Jazeera reported that a journalist was wounded in an Israeli settler attack in Al-Mughayyir, Ramallah.[207]
  • Wafa reported that an Israeli strike hit Asdaa, northwest of Khan Yunis, killing two civilians and wounding others.[208]
  • The IDF said that a reservist was critically injured by sniper fire in north Gaza. al-Qassam Brigades claimed responsibility.[209][210]
  • Lebanese media reported that one person was killed in an Israeli drone strike on a motorcycle in Yatar. The IDF said that it killed Hezbollah forces commander in Yatar and accused him of trying to restore Hezbollah's capabilities in the area.[211][212]
  • At least 10 Palestinians were killed after the Israeli forces opened fire on crowds of people while trying to get aid in Rafah by the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, an American and Israeli-backed humanitarian organization.[213] The IDF denied firing at Palestinians, saying that it had fired "warning shots" in an outside area to establish control over the situation.[214]

28 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 28 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours arrived at hospitals in Gaza, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,084.[215][a]
  • AFP reported that an Israeli strike hit a house in as-Saftawi, north Gaza, killing at least nine people and injuring a journalist.[216][217]
  • Al-Masirah reported that four Israeli attacks targeted the runway at Sanaa International Airport and a Yemenia plane. The IDF said that it hit the airport and targeted an aircraft used to transport Houthi militants.[218][219]
  • AFP reported that an Israeli strike hit central Gaza, killing six members of one family including children and injuring 15 others.[217]
  • Gaza Civil Defence said that an Israeli strike hit Khan Yunis, killing a civilian.[217]
  • The IDF said that it seized more than $2 million and detained more than 30 suspects in an operation one day prior in the West Bank against money exchange stores suspected of funding Hamas.[220]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck dozens of targets throughout Gaza in the last 48 hours including a rocket launcher used to fire projectiles towards Kissufim and its soldiers operating in Gaza, militants, buildings used by militant groups, anti-tank launch posts, weapon depots, and other infrastructure. It also said that it killed several militants planning to conduct a sniper and anti-tank missile attack on its forces in south Gaza.[221]
  • Gaza Humanitarian Foundation said that it opened its second aid distribution center in Rafah.[222]
  • Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Hamas' leader in the Gaza Strip, Muhammed Sinwar had been killed.[223]
  • The IDF said that it killed a Palestinian suspected of attacking soldiers using a "sharp object" in Jit, Qalqilya.[224]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a vehicle in al-Nafaq street of Gaza City, killing several people including a journalist.[225]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in Shuja'iyya killed a teenage boy.[225]
  • AP reported that four Palestinians died while storming a World Food Programme warehouse to get food.[203]

29 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 67 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours arrived at hospitals in Gaza, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,249.[226][a]
  • The IDF said that it demolished the house of a militant in the West Bank who conducted the Lehi Street bombing.[227]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in Bureij refugee camp killed at least 23 people, injuring others and several people went missing. Israeli forces were accused by local hospital of using internationally prohibited weapons in the attack.[228][229]
  • Al Jazeera reported that agricultural land was vandalised by settlers east of Yatta, Hebron.[230]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli drone strike in the outskirts of Nabatieh al-Fawqa killed one person.[231] The IDF said that it struck a Hezbollah militant in the vicinity of Beaufort Castle, Lebanon and accused him of trying to restore a major Hezbollah infrastructure in the area which had been struck several times in recent weeks.[232] But, a Lebanese official said that a municipal worker was killed in the attack.[233]
  • The Gaza Health Ministry said that Israeli forces ordered to evacuate Jabalia's al-Awda Hospital.[234]
  • The IDF said that it destroyed a Hamas attack tunnel with several exits, some of them booby-trapped, and killed a militant cell which emerged from one of the shafts during its operation in south Gaza.[235]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck dozens of targets in the last day including militant cells, buildings used by militant groups, observation and sniper posts, tunnels and other infrastructure. It also said that its ground troops killed several militants and destroyed weapons and other militant infrastructure, including tunnels.[236]
  • The infant of an Israeli pregnant woman who died in a shooting by a Palestinian militant in the West Bank died two weeks after emergency delivery.[237]
  • The IDF warned Palestinians in Nuseirat to stay away from several locations, saying that six prominent Hamas militants are hiding there and exploiting civilian infrastructure for combat.[238][239][240]
  • The Gaza Interior Ministry said that an Israeli strike hit Saraya Junction in central Gaza City, killing nine police officers.[241]
  • The IDF said that a Defence Ministry civilian contractor was killed during operations in Jabalia area after being by an explosive device apparently planted by militants.[242][243]
  • Gaza Humanitarian Foundation said that it opened a third aid distribution site in Gaza.[244]
  • NNA reported that a series of Israeli air strikes targeted areas in the vicinity of Beit Lif, Ramiyah, al-Bisariya, Wadi al-Safa and al-Sarira.[245] The IDF said that it hit Hezbollah infrastructure in Lebanon.[246]
  • The IDF said that air defences downed a ballistic missile fired towards Israel by the Houthis, who said they targeted Ben Gurion Airport.[247][248][249]
  • The IDF said that three soldiers were slightly injured by RPG fire while operating at a building in south Gaza. It also said that it killed militants behind the attack.[250]
  • Lebanese media reported an Israeli attack in the vicinity of Bnafoul.[251]
  • The IDF warned Palestinians to evacuate from Al-Atatra, Jabalia, and Shejaiya, Daraj Quarter, and Zaytun Quarter to head west, saying that it will expand its offensive activity in the areas to dismantle the capabilities of militant organizations.[252]
  • Al Jazeera reported that a 17-year-old was included among those wounded during an Israeli operation in Idna.[253]
  • The IDF said that a soldier from the 74th Battalion of the 188th Armored Brigade was critically injured in south Gaza one day prior due to an accidental misfire.[254]
  • Arab media reported that a second person was killed in an Israeli attack in south Lebanon.[255]

30 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 72 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,321.[256][a]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a home in Jabalia, killing at least 10 people.[257]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a home in Jabalia al-Balad area of north Gaza, killing a woman and injuring several others.[258]
  • Al Jazeera reported that a pregnant woman was slightly injured in a settler attack in Masafer Yatta.[259]
  • The al-Qassam Brigades released a video showing a group of masked and armed men attacked with explosives in Rafah, saying that they were working undercover for Israeli forces.[260]
  • The IDF said that it bombed a site used by Hezbollah to store weapons in Beqaa Valley and accused the group of attempting to restore the site.[261]
  • The IDF said that it destroyed a Hamas tunnel measuring a kilometer during recent operations in Khan Yunis and killed several militants inside.[262]
  • The IDF said that it arrested 80 "wanted individuals", seized several weapons and seven million shekels in militant funds.[263]
  • al-Qassam Brigades and al-Quds Brigades said they launched an anti-personnel grenade towards a building housing Israeli forces in an area southeast of Khan Yunis.[264]
  • Al Jazeera reported that olive trees were set on fire by Israeli settlers in Sinjil.[265]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck dozens of targets in Gaza in last day including militants, buildings used by militant groups, observation and sniper posts, tunnels and other militant infrastructure.[266]
  • The IDF said that it confiscated and destroyed more than 80 weapons and explosive devices which were located during operations in the Gaza in recent weeks.[267]

31 May

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 60 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,381.[268][a]
  • A woman was detained by Israeli forces from Anabta.[269]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli drone attack on a car in Deir ez-Zahrani killed a man. The IDF said that it killed a Hezbollah rocket commander in the Beaufort Castle area and accused him of trying to restore Hezbollah infrastructure.[270][271]
  • Two prisoners released as part of the January 2025 Gaza war ceasefire were rearrested by Israeli forces in Idna.[272]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a tent in Al-Shati refugee camp, killing five family members including a woman and her three children[273] and injured 13 more which are being treated in al-Shifa Hospital.[274]
  • al-Quds Brigades said that its mortar barrage targeted a gathering of Israeli forces and vehicles advancing southeast of Khan Yunis.[275]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck dozens of targets in the Gaza, including militants and infrastructure used by Hamas, and killed a prominent Hamas militant involved in producing weapons in a drone attack in Sabra, Gaza one day prior. It added that its Paratroopers Brigade killed a cell of four militants the previous day and destroyed several explosive devices in their operational area.[276]
  • The IDF said that it opened an investigation after its vehicles crashed into a Palestinian minibus in Jenin.[277]
  • Palestinians were reportedly assaulted by Israeli settlers in Khirbet al-Tuba, south of Hebron.[278]
  • The IDF said that three rockets launched from Gaza struck open areas in the vicinity of the border.[279]
  • The IDF and Shin Bet confirmed the death of leader of Hamas in the Gaza Strip Mohammed Sinwar, al-Qassam Brigades' Rafah Brigade commander Muhammad Shabana and the al-Qassam Brigades' South Khan Yunis Battalion commander.[280][281][282]
  • The IDF reissued warnings to evacuate Rafah and Khan Yunis.[283]

June

1 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 32 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,418.[284][a]
  • A doctor who lost nine of their 10 children in an Israeli strike on their house died from injuries sustained in the attack.[285]
  • The IDF said that it destroyed a Hamas tunnel measuring 700 metres, killed dozens of militants and destroyed more than 100 infrastructures used by militant groups in Khan Yunis.[286]
  • An Israeli drone strike hit a motorcycle in Arnoun, killing one person. The IDF said that it killed a militant from Hezbollah's anti-tank unit.[287][288]
  • At least 31 people were killed and more than 170 others were injured including women and children as they were on their way to a Gaza Humanitarian Foundation aid distribution site.[289][290][291] The IDF denied that fired towards civilians in the vicinity or within the site in the Rafah. An IDF official told the AP that soldiers fired warning shots towards several suspects advancing at them overnight.[289]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck dozens of targets in the Gaza Strip, including militants, booby-trapped structures and other buildings used by militant groups, tunnels, and sniper and anti-tank posts in the last day, and destroyed the remains of a booby-trapped building where a soldier was killed in May.[292]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli attack hit a car in Beit Lif, injuring one person.[293]
  • The IDF said that its drone attack killed an al-Qassam Brigades commander who led the deadliest attack on soldiers since the start of the war.[294]
  • The IDF said that air defences downed a ballistic missile fired towards Israel by the Houthis, who said that they targeted Ben Gurion Airport.[295][296]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a telecommunications hub in Bani Suheila, injuring two civilians.[297]
  • IDF chief Eyal Zamir ordered to expand ground offensive in additional areas of Gaza.[298]
  • The IDF struck al-Mawasi, with the Kuwaiti Field Hospital reporting one dead Palestinian and 30 others wounded. The IDF did not report this strike until questioned by the BBC, whereupon the IDF told the BBC that they had "wrongfully hit the Mawasi area" with artillery that "deviated" after "technical and operational errors".[299]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a vehicle on Debl road of Bint Jbeil District, killing one person.[293]
  • The IDF said that its drone killed a militant from Hezbollah's rocket unit.[300]
  • The IDF said that Palestinian gunmen shot at aid seekers in Khan Younis.[301]

2 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 51 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza and body of one person killed in a previous Israeli attack was recovered from the rubble in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,470.[302][a]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in Tel al-Hawa killed a child.[303]
  • Al Jazeera reported that nine people were arrested by Israeli forces from Dura, Hebron.[304]
  • Wafe reported that a boy died from injuries sustained in an Israeli strike which hit a house in Deir el-Balah and killed his other relatives.[305]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit the Israeli-designated humanitarian safe zone of al-Mawasi, killing four people and wounding dozens.[306]
  • The al-Quds Brigades claimed that it shelled Israeli forces near the customs police area southeast of Khan Yunis in cooperation with the Al-Aqsa Martyrs Brigades.[307]
  • The IDF said that it expanded its ground offensive in Gaza in past day, killed militants, destroyed many weapon depots and militant infrastructure, above and under ground. It also said that the IAF struck dozens of targets across Gaza in the past day, including militant cells, buildings used by militant groups, tunnels, weapon depots, and other infrastructure.[308]
  • Reuters reported that Israeli fire killed at least three people and injured dozens of others in the vicinity of a Gaza Humanitarian Foundation aid distribution site. The IDF said that it fired warning shots "to prevent several suspects approaching them".[309]
  • The al-Qassam Brigades said that it shelled a group of Israeli troops east of Al-Qarara two days prior. It also said that it targeted the Israeli Ein al-Thalatha site east of the same area using three short-range Rajum missiles.[310]
  • al-Qassam Brigades said that it engaged in "fierce clashes" with Israeli forces in north Gaza.[311]
  • The AP reported that an Israeli strike hit a residential building in Jabalia refugee camp, killing 14 people including seven children and five women.[312]
  • Gaza media reported that an Israeli strike in Deir al-Balah, killed at least three people. The IDF said that it targeted a Hamas command and control center.[313]
  • A 15-year-old teenager was shot and killed in Sinjil. The IDF said that it shot a Palestinian suspected of planning to hurl rocks towards a highway.[314][315]
  • Gaza medical sources said that an Israeli strike hit a home in Nuseirat refugee camp, reportedly killing a woman and her three children.[313]
  • The IDF ordered residents to evacuate from several blocks in west Khan Yunis.[316]
  • The IDF said that it downed a ballistic missile fired towards Israel by the Houthis, who said that they targeted Ben Gurion Airport.[317][318]
  • Al Jazeera reported that a 17-year-old teenager was wounded during an Israeli raid in Beit Furik.[319]

3 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 40 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,510.[320][a]
  • The IDF reported that three soldiers of the Givati Brigade were killed and two others were moderately injured the day prior by an explosive device while operating in Jabalia, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 423. Per an initial IDF investigation, five soldiers were in a Humvee in the area when they were hit by an explosive device planted there by militants.[321][322]
  • Gaza officials said that Israeli fire killed at least 27 people while waiting for aid distribution in Rafah. The IDF said that it opened fire on suspects 500 meters away from approved route.[323][324]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a home in Nuseirat refugee camp, killing a child and injuring others.[325]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck dozens of militant targets throughout Gaza, including militants, buildings used by militant groups, tunnels, and other infrastructure that threatened its forces. It also said that the 215th Artillery Regiment killed a Hamas militant at a weapons depot.[326]
  • Wafa reported that dozens of olive trees were destroyed by Israeli settlers in Kafr Malik.[327]
  • The IDF said that it downed a ballistic missile fired towards Israel by the Houthis, who said that they launched a hypersonic ballistic missile towards Ben Gurion airport.[328][329]
  • The IDF said that two rockets fired from southern Syria hit open areas in the Golan Heights. It responded by shelling the source of the launch.[330][331][332] Martyr Mohammed Deif Brigades said that it launched the rockets. The IDF later said that it conducted a wave of airstrikes across southern Syria targeting weapons owned by the Syrian transitional government,[333][334] which reported “significant human and material losses” in Daraa Governorate.[335]
  • Israeli forces dropped leaflets warning residents to leave their houses in some areas of Khan Yunis and move west, saying it would fight Hamas and other militant groups in these areas.[336]
  • al-Quds Brigades claimed that it destroyed an Israeli vehicle with a highly explosive barrel bomb in Qizan an-Najjar on 3 June.[337]

4 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 95 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours and two other bodies were recovered from rubble in Gaza, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,607.[320][a]
  • The IDF said that a reservist from the 6646th Battalion of the 646th Reserve Paratroopers Brigade was killed in combat in Shuja'iyya one day prior, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 425. Another reservist from the battalion was critically injured in the same incident.[338]
  • The IDF said that an explosive device was dropped with a drone by Hamas on forces operating in Jabalia one day prior, moderately injuring two soldiers from the Yahalom combat engineering unit and slightly injuring a Shin Bet officer.[339]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a school serving as shelter for displaced people in Khan Yunis, killing at least 18 people including children.[340]
  • Al Jazeera reported that 19 people including activists were detained by Israeli forces from the West Bank.[341]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in southwest Gaza City killed a man and his children.[342]
  • The Mujahideen Brigades said that an Israeli strike killed a member of its military council who was also its Central Governorate Brigade's head.[343]
  • The al-Quds Brigades claimed that it hit a group of Israeli soldiers southeast of Jabalia using two missiles.[344]
  • The al-Qassam Brigades claimed that it set fire to an Israeli tank south of Khan Yunis using an Al-Yassin 105 missile.[345]
  • Al Jazeera reported that a 70-year-old Gazan man died in Israeli custody.[346]
  • The IDF said that the IAF downed a drone fired towards Israel “from the east” above Be'er Milka. The Houthis said that they fired two drones towards Ben Gurion Airport, indicating that the second one likely crashed prior to reaching Israel.[347][348]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit al-Mawasi, killing three people including two children.[349]
  • Palestinian media reported that 35 people were wounded and buildings were set on fire in a settler attack in Deir Dibwan.[350][351]
  • The IDF warned against approaching areas in north Gaza, including Beit Lahia, Jabalia and Beit Hanoun, saying that they are combat zones.[352]
  • Gaza media source reported that Israel tried to kill Izz al-Din al-Haddad, who is one of the leading figures in Hamas.[353]

5 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 70 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,677.[354][a]
  • The bodies of hostages Gadi Haggai and Judih Weinstein were recovered by the IDF and Shin Bet from Gaza.[355]
  • Lebanese media reported that an Israeli drone attack hit a vehicle in Qalaouiyeh, injuring one person.[356][357]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli attack hit al-Nasser Street, in the vicinity of al-Shifa Hospital compound west of Gaza City, killing at least three people including children and women and injuring others.[358]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit Al-Ahli Arab Hospital, killing three journalists and critically wounded many others including a journalist.[359][360][361] The IDF said that it targeted a PIJ militant operating in a command and control center in the hospital.[362]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in the vicinity of Bureij wounded a child.[363]
  • Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed that his government armed clans in Gaza that opposed Hamas including one led by Yasser Abu Shabab.[364]
  • The IDF issued evacuation orders for four buildings and nearby areas in the southern suburbs of Beirut, saying that it will target Hezbollah "underground infrastructure". It later carried out the attacks.[365][366][367]
  • The IDF said that it downed a ballistic missile fired towards Israel by the Houthis, who said that they targeted Ben Gurion Airport.[368][369]
  • The IDF issued evacuation orders for two areas in Ain Qana, saying there are Hezbollah facilities in the area. A drone attack was later reported there.[370][371]
  • The Trump administration sanctioned four International Criminal Court judges for probing alleged Israeli war crimes in Gaza, the West Bank and East Jerusalem and alleged US war crimes in Afghanistan.[372][373][374]
  • Israeli forces detained seven journalists belonging to BBC News Arabic in the occupied Syrian town of Quneitra in the Golan Heights.[375]

6 June

  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit northwest of Khan Yunis, killing a child.[376]
  • The IDF ordered some residents to evacuate north Gaza.[377]
  • The IDF said that movement toward Gaza Humanitarian Foundation sites is only allowed between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. daily.[378]
  • The IDF said that four soldiers were killed and five were injured including one critically by a blast in a building in Khan Yunis, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 429. Per an initial IDF investigation, the soldiers entered a booby-trapped building to clear it of possible militant infrastructure and the blast caused the building to collapse on the soldiers.[379][380][381]
  • The al-Qassam Brigades said that it, along with the al-Quds Brigades shelled Israeli forces south of Khan Yunis.[382]
  • AFP reported that an Israeli strike in Jabalia killed 11 people.[383]

7 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 95 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 48 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,772.[384][a]
  • The IDF said that a reservist from the 646th Paratroopers Brigade was moderately injured by a shell launched by militants in Shuja'iyya. It issued evacuation orders for a small area in Gaza City after the attack which was already covered in an earlier evacuation order.[385]
  • The body of Thai hostage Natthapong Pinta was recovered by Israel.[386]
  • Palestinian media reported that an Israeli strike hit a tent camp in Khan Yunis, killing 12 people and injuring almost 40 others.[387]
  • An Israeli strike hit a building in Sabra, Gaza, reportedly killing at least 16 people including children and women, injuring at least 50 others and trapping almost 85 under the rubble.[388][389][390] Mujahideen Brigades chief As'ad Abu Shari'a, whom the IDF said that participated in the 7 October attacks, was killed in this strike.[386][391]
  • AP reported that an Israeli strike hit an apartment in north Gaza, killing seven people including five children and a woman.[386]
  • AP reported that at least six people were killed while on their way to obtain food assistance. The IDF said that despite earlier warnings that the area is an active combat zone between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m, several suspects tried to approach its forces operating in the Tel al-Sultan area overnight “in a manner that posed a threat to the troops”. The army also said that its forces called to drive them away but as they continued advancing they fired warning shots. It added that it is aware of reports of casualties. An unnamed IDF official said that warning shots were fired almost one kilometer from Gaza Humanitarian Foundation aid distribution site.[386]
  • The IDF ordered residents to evacuate Abd al-Rahman neighborhood of Gaza City and al-Nahda neighborhood of Jabalia refugee camp.[392][393]
  • The IDF, Shin Bet and Israeli police said that they detained a suspected prominent militant from a network in Burqin and thwarted an imminent attack.[394]
  • The al-Quds Brigades said that it targeted Israeli forces and vehicles in an area northeast of Khan Yunis and in Tal al-Zaatar area of Jabalia refugee camp.[395]

8 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 108 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,880.[396][a]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit tents in al-Mawasi area of Khan Yunis, killing five people including two girls.[397]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in the Al-Atatra neighborhood of Beit Lahia injured an elderly man and a girl.[398]
  • The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said that an Israeli attack hit a vehicle in Beit Jinn, killing one person and wounding two others. The IDF said that it targeted a Hamas militant.[399][400]
  • The IDF said that it killed a Hamas-run police station chief who participated in the Nova music festival massacre in an airstrike on 31 May, and targeted dozens of Hamas militants in airstrikes in Khan Yunis. It added that a killed several militants at a command center and struck dozens more targets, including weapon depots, tunnels, and militants in airstrikes in the last day.[401]
  • Reservists from the IDF's Hasmonean Brigade entered Gaza for the first time to participate in the offensive.[402]
  • At least 12 people were killed as they headed towards two Gaza Humanitarian Foundation aid distribution points. The IDF said that it fired warning shots towards those who approached it.[403]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli drone strike hit a motorcycle on a road between Chehabiyeh and Kfar Dounin, in the vicinity of Tyre, killing one person.[404]
  • The IDF said that it found leader of Hamas in the Gaza Strip Mohammed Sinwar's body in an "underground passageway beneath the European Hospital" in Khan Yunis.[405]

9 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 47 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 54,927.[406][a]
  • The IDF, Shin Bet and Israeli police said that they arrested 35 suspects from an explosives laboratory that it destroyed in Tulkarm and seized weapons and funds related to militant activity.[407]
  • The passengers of the Madleen were intercepted by Israeli forces on its way to the Gaza Strip while under a blockade with activists including Greta Thunberg detained. Israeli authorities stated that all of the activists would be returned to their home countries.[408][409][410]
  • The IDF said that it found and destroyed a tunnel measuring a mile in Khan Yunis. It also said that it destroyed a weapons depot and dozens of buildings which had been booby-trapped with five tonnes of explosives by Hamas.[411]
  • The IDF said that it killed 15 militants in clashes in Khan Yunis in the last day, and struck dozens more targets, including tunnels and militants throughout Gaza.[412]
  • Lebanese media reported that an Israel drone attack hit a car in Al-Numairiyah.[413]
  • Gaza's Health Ministry and local hospitals reported that 14 people were killed while heading towards a Gaza Humanitarian Foundation food distribution center.[414]
  • The IDF issued evacuation orders for north Gaza, including Jabalia to move to Gaza City.[415]
  • The IDF ordered to evacuate Hudaydah Port, Port of Salif and Ras Isa Port, saying that they are used by the Houthis for militant activities.[416][417]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike in Tuffah killed three paramedics and a journalist.[418]

10 June

  • The Israeli Navy launched attacks on Houthi territory in Yemen for the first time, targeting the port of Hodeidah.[419][420]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a tent in al-Mawasi, killing three people.[421]
  • The IDF said that air defences downed one rocket fired from both Gaza towards south Israel. It later issued evacuation order for four neighborhoods in north Gaza to move to Gaza City, saying that the rocket was launched from the area.[422][423][424]
  • The IDF said it destroyed more than 1,200 militant infrastructures in Khuza'a, Khan Yunis.[425]
  • Thirty-six people were reportedly killed and 207 others were wounded while waiting for aid in the vicinity of Netzarim Corridor. The IDF said that it fired warning shots towards "suspects who were advancing in the area of Wadi Gaza and posed a threat to the troops".[426][427][428]
  • The IDF said a drone attack targeted two Hamas militants disguised as women during recent operations in north Gaza. It also said that it found a rocket launcher and other weapons owned by Hamas.[429]
  • The IDF said that two Palestinians were killed and four soldiers were wounded while trying to snatch a soldier's gun in Nablus.[430]
  • Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Norway and the UK announced sanctions against Israeli far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir and Israeli far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich for "inciting violence against Palestinians in the West Bank".[431][432] In response, Smotrich ordered the cancellation of a waiver allowing bank ties between Israel and the Palestinian Authority.[433][434]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli drone strike in the vicinity of Shebaa, killed two people and injured another person. The IDF said that it killed a Hezbollah militant and a Lebanese Resistance Brigades militant and accused them of violating the ceasefire.[435][436]
  • The IDF said that it downed a ballistic missile fired towards Israel by the Houthis.[437]

11 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 120 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,104.[438][a]
  • Israeli forces opened fire in the vicinity of an aid distribution center near Netzarim Corridor, reportedly killing at least 25 people and injuring more than 100 others. The IDF said that it fired warning shots towards suspects who approached it and “posed a threat".[439][440]
  • One person was killed and at least 10 others including two teenage brothers were detained by Israeli forces from West Bank. PIJ said that the person killed in Tammun was one of its senior members. The IDF said that it also arrested two other militants from a local network in an operation jointly conducted with Shin Bet and Israeli police special operations unit in the same area.[441][442][443]
  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit near the Jordanian field hospital west of Khan Yunis, injuring a Jordanian doctor.[444][445]
  • The al-Quds Brigades said that it engaged in "fierce clashes" with Israeli forces in an area north of Khan Yunis.[446]
  • The al-Qassam Brigades claimed that it killed an IDF soldier in the vicinity of Abasan al-Kabira.[447]
  • The IDF said that two soldiers were moderately injured during a gun battle with a militant in Khan Yunis.[448]
  • An Israeli drone attack hit a car in Beit Lif, killing at least one person and injuring three others. The IDF said that it killed a Radwan Force militant.[449][450][451]
  • The bodies of Israeli hostages Yair Yaakov and Aviv Atzili were recovered by the IDF in a joint operation with Shin Bet.[452][453]
  • The IDF said that an officer and a soldier were moderately injured after an RGP hit a tank they were in during combat in Khan Yunis.[454][455]

12 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 29 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,207.[456][a]
  • The IDF said that it killed two militants and arrested 10 wanted Palestinians in a nearly 30-hour raid in central Nablus. It added that it located a number of weapons, including makeshift guns, and ammunition, and "much inciting material".[457]
  • Gaza Humanitarian Foundation accused Hamas of killing its eight employees and injuring multiple others in attack on a bus while traveling to a food distribution point west of Khan Yunis. However, International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement denied GHF's claim that Red Cross was involved in evacuating its killed and injured employees.[458][459] A Hamas-run police force unit claimed that it killed 12 Palestinian members of the Israeli-backed Popular Forces.[460]
  • The IDF said that it arrested suspected Hamas militants from Beit Jinn.[461]
  • The IDF said that it killed a cell of Hamas militants which injured two soldiers in an RPG attack in Khan Yunis one day prior and killed several militants moving weapons in a drone strike.[462]
  • CIA analyst Asif William Rahman was sentenced to three years' imprisonment in a US court for leaking classified documents about Israeli strike plans on Iran.[463]
  • The IDF released documents allegedly drawn up by Hamas, saying that it proves that Hamas maintained a policy of confiscating 15%-25% of aid.[464]
  • The IDF said that it hit Hamas militants operating in a weapons manufacturing plant in Al-Shati refugee camp.[465]
  • The IDF said that it "neutralized" a Palestinian militant who opened fire on its forces in the vicinity of Hermesh.[466]
  • Palestinian media reported that Israeli fire killed almost 32 people as they approached a Gaza Humanitarian Foundation aid site. The IDF said that it fired “warning shots” towards a crowd of Gazans which approached them and “posed a threat”.[467]
  • The IDF issued new evacuation orders for south Gaza to move west and slightly expanded a no-go zone, saying that it is operating in these areas to dismantle militant capabilities.[468]
  • Lebanese media reported Israeli strikes in the vicinity of Al-Baisariyah and Tebna, south of Sidon.[469]
  • An Israeli drone strike hit a motorcycle in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, killing one person. NNA also reported several Israeli airstrikes throughout south Lebanon.[470]
  • The IDF issued evacuation orders for several neighborhoods in central Gaza.[471]

13 June

  • The IDF said that two soldiers from the 601st Combat Engineering Battalion were critically injured during a gun battle with militants during combat in north Gaza.[472]
  • The IDF reiterated its evacuation orders for a large part of Gaza.[473]
  • A ballistic missile was fired from Yemen to Israel.[474] The IDF said that the missile landed in the vicinity of Sa'ir.[475] Missile shrapnel wounded at least five Palestinians including three children.[476]

14 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 90 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 48 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,297.[477][a]
  • The IDF said that it intercepted three drones apparently fired from Yemen.[478]
  • The IDF said that two rockets fired from Gaza hit open areas in the vicinity of the border fence.[479]
  • The IDF issued evacuation orders for Khan Yunis, Abasan al-Kabira and Bani Suhaila to move west to humanitarian area, saying it would forcefully work against militant organisations in the area.[480]
  • The IDF said that two rockets fired from south Gaza towards south Israel hit open areas.[481]
  • Gaza health officials reported that Israeli strikes in Khan Yunis killed at least 16 people including five women.[482]
  • Local hospitals said that Israeli fire killed at least 15 people near a Gaza Humanitarian Foundation aid distribution point in the vicinity of Netzarim Corridor. The IDF said that it opened fire on an individual after he advanced towards its forces and ignored warning shots fired in the vicinity of a group.[480]
  • The IDF said that a Houthi leadership meeting in Yemen including Houthi forces's commander Muhammad Abd Al-Karim Al-Ghamari was targeted in a strike in Yemen.[483][484]

15 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 65 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,362.[485][a]
  • The IDF said that a commander from the Kfir Brigade was killed during combat in south Gaza, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 430. Another soldier was slightly wounded in the same incident.[486][487]
  • Al Jazeera reported that lands in Huwara were ignited by Israeli settlers before opening fire on civil defense personnel approaching to extinguish the fire, while the head of the village of Khirbet Ibziq, northeast of Tubas, said Israeli settlers stole a water tanker in the area at dawn. Israeli forces installed an iron gate at the entrance of Hizma, in the northeast of East Jerusalem, to restrict the movement of Palestinians in the area.[488]
  • Medics said that an Israeli strike hit a home in Nuseirat refugee camp, killing at least 11 people.[489]
  • The IDF said that one rocket fired from south Gaza struck an open area in south Israel.[490]

16 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 68 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,432.[491][a]
  • Israel announced that a captain of the Golani Brigade who was also a Shin Bet combat commander was killed by an explosive device in Khan Yunis, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 431.[492][493]

17 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 61 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,493.[494][a]
  • The IDF said that a soldier from the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion was killed during combat in south Gaza one day prior, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 432. It also said that 10 others were injured, including four critically in the same incident. Per an initial IDF investigation, the soldiers were in an armored personnel carrier while operating in Khan Yunis, when a militant placed an explosive device on the outside of the vehicle.[495]
  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that Israeli fire killed at least 51 people in Khan Yunis. The IDF said that it may have opened fire on Gazans who approached its forces.[496][497]
  • The IDF said that it demolished the house of a Palestinian militant who killed an Israeli boy in a gun attack on a bus in the West Bank in 2024.[498]
  • The IDF said that it advanced to Kafr Jabalia area of Jabalia for the first time in its ground offensive. It also said that it killed numerous militants and destroyed several tunnel shafts and rocket launchers.[499]
  • The IDF said that two rockets fired from south Gaza fell in open areas in south Israel.[500]
  • Middle East Eye reported that an Israeli strike hit a home in Bureij refugee camp, killing at least four people including children and women.[501]
  • The IDF issued a new evacuation order in south Gaza, expanding a large no-go zone slightly.[502]
  • Tunnel under the European hospital in Gaza, was sealed using concrete to avoid damage to the hospital.[503]

18 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 144 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,637.[504][a]
  • The IDF said that it opened fire and "neutralized" a Palestinian man who tried to stab soldiers and snatch a gun in al-Walaja.[505]
  • Wafa reported that an Israeli strike hit a house in Maghazi refugee camp, killing 10 people including a woman and her children.[506]
  • Wafa reported that an Israeli strike hit a tent in al-Attar area of Khan Yunis, killing five people including a woman and two children and injured others.[506]
  • The IDF said that it launched an airstrike on three militants approaching its forces in Jabalia, targeted a building used by Hamas in the area, killed two “suspects who posed a threat”, directed a strike on Hamas tunnel infrastructure in central Gaza and destroyed a booby trapped building in Khan Yunis.[507]
  • IDF spokesperson Effie Defrin said the IAF struck more than 75 targets in Gaza in last day. He also said that “in the Gaza Strip, we are fighting according to a structured plan with four divisions".[508]
  • The IDF said that a soldier from the 603rd Combat Engineering Battalion was killed during combat in south Gaza, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 433. Per an initial IDF investigation the soldier was killed by sniper fire in Khan Yunis.[509]
  • The IDF said that a rocket launched from Gaza fell in an open area in the vicinity of Nirim.[510]
  • The IDF said that a reservist from the 8105th Battalion of the 646th Reserve Paratroopers Brigade was critically injured in south Gaza.[511]
  • The IDF said that it killed a Hezbollah commander in a drone strike in Barish and accused him of trying to restore Hezbollah artillery.[512]

19 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 69 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,706.[513][a]
  • The IDF said that it demolished the house of a militant who conducted a shooting at Gitti Avissar intersection on 29 November 2024.[514]
  • The IDF said that it killed the commander of Hezbollah's anti-tank unit in Shebaa in a drone strike in south Lebanon and accused him of violating the ceasefire.[515]
  • Lebanese media reported that an Israeli drone attack hit a car near Houla, killing one person. The IDF said that it killed a Hezbollah militant involved in efforts to restore Hezbollah infrastructure in the area.[516][517]
  • AFP reported that Israeli fire killed at least 15 people in the Netzarim Corridor. The IDF said that it fired "warning shots" towards "suspects" approaching it, however that it was "not aware of any injured individuals".[518] Al Jazeera updated the casualties to 22.[519]
  • Medics said that an Israeli strike hit a tent in Al-Shati refugee camp, killing 19 people including children and women.[520]
  • Medics said that an Israeli strike hit Jabalia, killing 14 people.[520]

20 June

  • Al Jazeera reported that an Israeli strike hit a house in al-Ma'askar area of Deir el-Balah, killing at least 12 people and injuring others.[521][522][523]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli drone targeted a car in the town of Al-Aabbassiyah in the Tyre District of Lebanon, killing one person.[524]
  • The IDF said that a rocket launched from Gaza hit an open area in the vicinity of Be'eri.[525]
  • The IDF said that it killed a senior Mujahideen Brigades commander in a strike in central Gaza in this week. It also said it struck approximately 300 militant targets in Gaza, including militants, buildings used by militant groups, weapon depots, and missile and sniper posts in the last week.[526]
  • The IDF said that it killed the commander of Hezbollah's firepower unit in the Litani river area, in a drone strike in Shabriha in the vicinity of Tyre and accused him of violating the ceasefire.[527]
  • The IDF said that it killed al-Qassam Brigades finance chief who was a former aide to former Brigade deputy chief Marwan Issa in an airstrike in central Gaza in this week.[528]
  • The IDF said that the IAF struck Hezbollah targets including rocket launchers and weapons caches in south Lebanon and accused the group of violating ceasefire.[529]
  • Gaza Health Ministry said that Israeli fire killed at least 25 people south of the Netzarim Corridor. The IDF said that it fired warning shots towards suspected militants who approached it. It also said that an Israeli aircraft then struck and killed the suspects. It added that it was aware of others being hurt in the incident.[523]
  • Al Jazeera reported that Israeli forces carried out operations in the towns of 'Arura and Abwein, as well as the Nubani farms in Ramallah. The Palestinian Information Center reported that Israeli forces turned some of the houses owned by Palestinians into military barracks.[530]

21 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 202 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 48 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,908.[531][a]
  • NNA reported that an Israeli drone attack hit a motorcycle in Baraachit, killing one person. The IDF said that it killed a Hezbollah militant.[532][533]
  • The IDF said that its naval vessel targeted a facility belonging to the Radwan Force in Naqoura after gathering intelligence including from the interrogation of an arrested Hezbollah militant.[534]
  • Israeli settlers with protection from the IDF attacked the village of Deir Jarir, east of Ramallah, local residents confronted the settlers which prompted the soldiers to fire live round and stun grenades without any casualties reported.[535]

22 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 51 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,959.[536][a]
  • The remains of hostages Ofra Keidar, Yonatan Samerano, and Shay Levinson were recovered by Israel from Gaza.[537]
  • The IDF announced that it, Israel Border Police and Shin Bet expanded operations in the West Bank over the weekend.[538]
  • The New Arab reported that an Israeli strike hit a house in Nuseirat refugee camp, killing a Gaza Civil Defence member.[536]

23 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 39 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 55,998.[539][a]
  • Wafa reported that an Israeli strike in Gaza City killed three people including a child.[540]
  • NNA reported that Israeli air strikes hit the outskirts of several areas in southern Lebanon including Zrariyeh, Kfrar Milki and Ansar.[541]
  • The IDF said that it destroyed 2.5 kilometers of Hamas tunnels while operating in Kafr Jabalia, north Gaza.[542]
  • The IDF said that it conducted strikes targeting Hezbollah military sites including rocket launchers and weapon depots north of the Litani River and accused the group of violating the ceasefire.[543]
  • A 13-year-old Palestinian teenager died from injuries sustained from shots fired by Israeli forces in Kafr Malik.[544]

24 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 79 bodies of people killed in Israeli attacks arrived at hospitals throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 56,077.[545][a]
  • Lebanese media reported that an Israeli drone attack hit a car in the vicinity of Kfardajal, killing three people.[546]
  • Medics said that an Israeli strike in Sabra, Gaza killed 10 people.[547]
  • Medics said that Israeli gunfire in Khan Yunis killed 11 people.[547]
  • The IDF dropped leaflets over several parts of northern Gaza ordering residents to move south.[547]
  • al-Quds Brigades claimed that it inflicted casualties by shelling a gathering of Israeli forces in south Khan Yunis.[548]
  • al-Qassam Brigades claimed that it inflicted casualties by launching rocket-propelled grenades and opening fire at Israeli forces sheltering in a home in south Khan Yunis.[549]

25 June

  • The Gaza Health Ministry reported that at least 74 people were killed in Israeli attacks throughout Gaza in the past 24 hours and bodies of five people killed in earlier attacks were recovered, increasing its count of the Palestinian death toll in Gaza to 56,156.[550][a]
  • Seven Israeli soldiers from the 605th Combat Engineering Battalion were killed during combat in south Gaza, increasing the IDF death toll in Gaza to 440. Per an initial IDF investigation, a militant planted an explosive device on a Puma armored combat engineering vehicle the soldiers were in while they were driving in Khan Yunis. Two soldiers were injured, one critically and one slightly by RPG fire in a separate incident in Khan Yunis.[551][552]
  • Palestinian media reported that shots fired by Israel Border Police killed an elderly woman during a raid in Shu'fat Camp.[553][554]
  • The IDF said that it downed a drone apparently fired from Yemen prior to entering Israeli airspace.[555]
  • Lebanese media reported that an Israeli drone attack targeted the vicinity of Al-Mansouri, injuring at least one person.[556]
  • The IDF said that it and Shin Bet detained 20 suspected militants during overnight operations in the West Bank. It also said that materials used for producing explosives, weapons, and tens of thousands of shekels were found and seized during the operation. It added that it arrested a weapons dealer from Jenin.[557]
  • Gaza health officials said that 33 people reportedly died while attempting to access food. The IDF said that it fired warning shots towards people it said approached its forces in a suspicious manner.[558]

26 June
